m2-determinism.title: Determinism: two builds from unchanged source are byte-identical
m2-determinism.imperative: Add a determinism check: build twice from unchanged source into two fresh trees and require the two trees to be byte-identical; any non-empty diff is the failure (report every differing path, not a boolean). Add a test named for determinism over a synthetic repo. Prove it red by making the renderer non-deterministic (a set-ordered listing) and observing a non-empty diff with a non-zero exit. Restore the renderer byte-exact.

preconditions.satisfied_by: m1-harness complete: CHECKS registry + non-zero exit landed.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: determinism check observed failing under a deliberately non-deterministic renderer -- manual attest
postconditions.satisfied_by: RED observed end to end. Mutation applied to a COPY of scripts/code_map (render.py): 'ext = sorted({...})' -> 'ext = list({...})', a set of import names printed in hash order. Rebuilt through the copy, then 'python -m scripts.code_map check --root <fixture>' -> exit 1, 'FAIL deterministic-rebuild: 1 / pkg.wide/INDEX.md: same length, different bytes'. Positive control in the same shape: the UNMUTATED copy exits 0, so the red is attributable to the mutation and not to running from a copy. The two builds run in separate processes with PYTHONHASHSEED pinned to 0 and 1 -- a single process shares one seed, so an in-process double build cannot see this class of defect at all.

postconditions.statement: determinism check green on unchanged source

check.command: env -u FORCE_COLOR -u PYTHONIOENCODING python -m pytest tests/test_code_map.py -k determinism -q --color=no

constraints: no timings may enter any run report -- they would break this diff

Add a test; prove it red by mutating the renderer's inbound accumulation (drop `reads`, or attribute to the wrong module). Restore byte-exact. State plainly in the module docstring what this check does NOT prove.

postconditions.satisfied_by: Two silent mutations of render.py, each killed with a non-zero exit. (1) drop-reads: 'if p in ("calls", "reads")' -> 'if p in ("calls",)'. check -> exit 1, 'FAIL inbound-attribution: 1 / pkg.callee/target.md: page says 4 inbound sites, the store has 5'. (2) wrong-caller: 'inbound[o][intern(modof(s))] += 1' -> 'modof(o)'. check -> exit 1, 'page says 1 calling modules, the store has 2' + 'page names [] as callers, the store has [pkg.far]'. m4-selfconsistency.title: A page's referenced-by count agrees with its own list; the entity/symbol join is sane
m4-selfconsistency.imperative: Add two page-local checks that need no store: (a) a `referenced by: N sites in M modules (...)` line must not name more modules than it counts, must name distinct modules, and M may exceed the named list by at most one (the page's own module, which the renderer omits from the list); (b) every entity page's title key must agree with the store symbol the renderer joined it to on its leaf name -- a mis-join is then visible without trusting the join. why_trail.why: Context loaded and ground truth measured before writing anything: a fresh full build of this repo takes 7.5s and reports pages=3648 modules=112 entities=3536 entity_pages=3536, so pages-1-modules=3535 != 3536 -- the handoff's RED invariant reproduces exactly, and map/scripts.run_skill_eval/ holds Verdict.md with no verdict.md beside it. checks.py today prints and returns a literal 0.

checks.py rewritten around a MapUnderCheck that reads the stores and the page tree directly rather than through render.load_stores, plus a CHECKS registry whose run() returns 1 when any check fails. A missing page tree or missing store is now a FAILURE, not a skip -- the vacuous-pass shape test_mutation_floor pins for map_orient. First real check: no-empty-pages (tc26).

Determinism lands as two builds in SEPARATE processes with different hash seeds, compared byte-for-byte; tree_diff names every differing path rather than returning a boolean. The separate-process detail is load-bearing: a string hash seed is fixed for a process's life, so two builds inside one process share it and a hash-ordered listing looks perfectly stable. Nothing in the shipped tree was mutated -- the attack runs against a copied package, which also gives every later check a red proof harness.
